events.stem:
The kinetic molecular theory provides a theoretical framework to describe the behavior of ideal gases.

Which of the following statements about the postulates of the kinetic theory of gases is/are correct? (One or more options may be correct.)
(A) The assumption of no intermolecular attraction fails for real gases at high pressure and low temperature.
(B) Gas molecules are assumed to attract one another strongly.
(C) At a given temperature, the average kinetic energy of the molecules depends on the identity of the gas.
(D) The volume of the molecules themselves is assumed to be negligible compared with the volume of the container.

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working: Kinetic molecular theory postulates for ideal gases: (1) Gas molecules are point particles with negligible volume compared to container volume → statement D is correct. (2) No intermolecular forces (no attraction/repulsion) → at high pressure and low temperature real gases deviate because attractions become significant, so statement A correctly describes failure of the no-attraction assumption for real gases under those conditions. (3) Statement B claims strong attraction, which contradicts ideal gas assumption; incorrect. (4) Average kinetic energy depends only on temperature (same for all ideal gases), not identity; statement C is false. Therefore correct statements are A and D.
